---
title: "A random-criterion representation of weighted risk"
subtitle: "4.8 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 11–12"
description: "Drawing one criterion for a fixed report reproduces its weighted risk on average."
---

Consider a fixed grade report and draw one criterion, with chances given by the error weights. Evaluate the whole
report on that criterion. The average risk over these draws equals the weighted risk computed directly. The
draw applies to all units and all pairs, preserving their joint distribution within the chosen criterion.
The report is already fixed when the criterion is drawn.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Weighted report.** Both calculations give risk .0933. The criterion contributions are .0453 and .0480.
  Select a criterion column to inspect its whole vector. Report 1/1/1/1/2/3 stays fixed.
- **Certain opposition.** The two directions each cost .5000, while withholding costs .3000. Both criteria
  distinguish the units with certainty. The same criterion choice applies to both units and every reported pair.
- **Three actions tie.** All 3 actions cost .5000. Other reports share the weighted minimum even though their risks differ by criterion. Each report is evaluated before a criterion is drawn.
- **Two against one.** The cheaper direction costs .3333, the reverse .6667, and withholding .4000. A certain
  two-against-one split can favor disclosure. The adjacent one-third boundary preset retains both actions sharing
  the minimum instead of treating equality as a strict preference.
- **Zero error weight.** The cheaper weighted direction costs 0, although the ignored criterion’s own risk
  is 1.0000. Its selection chance is 0, so this branch contributes nothing. The column still shows how the report fares on that criterion.
- **No-cap coherence.** Among all 4,683 reports, 1/2/2/3/4/5 states 14 pairs with risk .1275. It states A above C
  with weighted error .3803 and B above D with .3813, both above τ .35. There is no grade cap in this example.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The criterion draw is independent of the targets conditional on the supplied information. Its probabilities
are the weights in the loss. In postrank, a strict direction counts as wrong when the target values are equal.
The link to KRW's strict-count objective requires matching the law, targets, orientation, units and report
family, as well as the affine and equality conditions of that result.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The fixed default report reproduces the two calculations; small floating-point rounding differences do not change
their algebraic identity.

```r
library(postrank)
ev <- postrank_evaluate(c(A=1L,B=1L,C=1L,D=1L,E=2L,F=3L), pr_tutorial$two, weights=c(score_A=.5,score_B=.5), tau=.2)
sum(c(.5,.5)*ev$criterion_risk); ev$weighted_risk
```
:::

Standalone: [open this app](../../embed/criterion-mixture.html), for example `?preset=coherence&theme=dark`.
